1. (Currently amended) A method of treating a brain, comprising: inserting an elongated device into the brain to create a path __between non-adjacent tissue structures__; radially expanding the device to create a working channel along the path; and introducing a medical element into the working channel to perform a medical procedure on the brain __while maintaining separation of the non-adjacent tissue structures__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is an instrument __selected from the group consisting of a suction device, a cutting instrument, a grasping instrument, and a visualization device__.

3. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising creating an opening in a cranium, and inserting the elongated device through the opening __such that the device maintains contact with tissue layers on both sides of the path__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers within the brain __and maintaining the device in a position that prevents collapse of the tissue layers__.

6. (Original) The method of claim 1, further comprising radially contracting and removing the device from the brain.

7. (Currently amended) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the device against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially reinforcing the device against the tissue __by maintaining radial pressure throughout the procedure__; and introducing a medical element through the device to perform a medical procedure on the tissue __while the device maintains the working channel open__.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is an instrument __selected from the group consisting of a suction device, a cutting instrument, a grasping instrument, and a visualization device__.

9. (Original) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers __and maintaining the device in a position that prevents collapse of the tissue layers__.

11. (Original) The method of claim 7, further comprising radially contracting and removing the device from the tissue.

12. (Original) The method of claim 7, further comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding.

13. (Currently amended) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device, having a first radially expandable body, surrounded by a stent, which is surrounded by a second radially expandable body, into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the second expandable body against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially expanding the first expandable body to radially expand the stent to reinforce the second expandable body against the tissue; radially contracting and removing the first expandable body to create a working channel through the stent __while maintaining the stent in an expanded configuration__; introducing a medical element through the channel to perform a medical procedure on the tissue __while the stent maintains the working channel open__; and radially contracting the second expandable body and removing the device from the tissue __in a manner that preserves tissue integrity__.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is an instrument __selected from the group consisting of a suction device, a cutting instrument, a grasping instrument, and a visualization device__.

15. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers __and maintaining the device in a position that prevents collapse of the tissue layers__.

17. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding.
